title: Verdict due today at inquest into Ontario man who died after hit with Taser
article: A coroner's jury is set to deliver its verdict today on just what role a Taser played in the death of a 27-year-old Ontario man at the hands of police.
Aron Firman's death in June 2010 has been called an "index case" by Ontario's top pathologist, who has testified that the stun gun was a key factor in the fatality.
Presiding coroner William Lucas warned the five-member jury panel on Friday not to resort to an "undetermined" cause of death as a matter of convenience.
The jury may put forward recommendations on what can be done to prevent similar deaths in the future.
Firman, a man with schizophrenia, died after an encounter with Ontario Provincial Police in Collingwood, Ont.

The inquest has heard vastly different testimony from experts. Some have suggested the use of a Taser on Firman was a key factor in his death, while others argued the stun gun had little to do with the fatality.
Ontario's police watchdog cleared the officers involved of any wrongdoing, but also said the Taser's deployment caused Firman's death.
The family hopes the inquest will lead to better guidelines for the use of Tasers by authorities and improved response techniques for when police deal with agitated mentally ill people.

The lawyer representing Taser International has suggested Firman could have died from cardiac arrhythmia brought on by "excited delirium" - a condition sometimes cited as a cause of death in people using cocaine or those with severe mental illness.
